title: Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Terminal 5 Changi capacity
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong broke ground on Terminal 5, which will raise Changi's capacity by about 50 million passengers a year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong just broke ground on Terminal 5, which will increase Changi’s capacity by about 50 million passengers a year.

sections.label: Singapore SAF uplift targets
sections.summary: Singapore has set a 1% SAF uplift target by 2026, aiming for 3% to 5% by 2030, subject to global developments and SAF availability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: To anchor supply resilience, Singapore has set a 1% SAF uplift target by 2026, with the goal to raise this to 3% to 5% by 2030, subject to global developments and the wider availability of SAF.

sections.label: Fixed cost envelope model
sections.summary: Singapore will adopt a fixed cost envelope model funded through a SAF levy instead of mandating SAF, which could impose unpredictable costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Simply mandating the use of SAF would impose unpredictable and unsustainable costs on airlines and passengers as SAF prices may vary significantly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This is why Singapore will adopt a fixed cost envelope model, funded through a SAF levy.

sections.label: Levy quantum stays fixed
sections.summary: The levy quantum for that year will not change even if the actual SAF premium differs from the projection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Importantly, the levy quantum for that year will not change even if the actual SAF premium differs from our projection.

sections.label: Aggregating SAF demand centrally
sections.summary: Airlines can plan with confidence and passengers and shippers can expect predictable charges, with SAF demand aggregated and centrally procured.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Airlines can plan with confidence, and passengers and shippers can expect predictable and stable charges, instead of facing sharp and unpredictable fluctuations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We will also aggregate SAF demand across airlines and centrally procure SAF using the SAF levy collected.

sections.label: Clause 9 SAF levy
sections.summary: Clause 9 provides for the SAF levy on passengers, cargoes and flights departing Singapore, payable to CAAS and paid into the SAF Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Clause 9 of the Bill provides for the SAF levy to be payable in respect of passengers, cargoes and flights departing from an airport in Singapore to land in a place outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Clause 9 also provides that the SAF levy is payable to the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The amount or rate will be prescribed in the Order and must be paid into the SAF Fund.

sections.label: SAF Fund and its purposes
sections.summary: New sections 25C and 25D establish the SAF Fund from SAF levies, interest and penalties, and list its purposes including procuring SAF and SAF EAs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The new section 25C establishes the SAF Fund, which comprises, among other moneys, all the SAF levies collected, and all interests and penalties imposed in relation to the SAF levies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The new section 25D sets out an exhaustive list of the purposes of the SAF Fund, which includes procuring SAF and SAF EAs and paying for the costs of procuring, managing and allocating SAF and SAF EAs.

sections.label: SAF cost and production share
sections.summary: SAF remains three to five times more expensive than conventional jet fuel, and IATA states global production was 0.2% of jet fuel consumption in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Yet, SAF today remains three to five times more expensive than conventional jet fuel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to the International Air Transport Association (IATA), global production accounted for only 0.2% of jet fuel consumption in 2023.

sections.label: SAF capacity and ICAO target
sections.summary: Shell suspended its Rotterdam SAF facility, world SAF capacity is about 600 million litres a year, and meeting ICAO's 5% target by 2030 needs a 50-fold increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Just this year, Shell suspended plans for its 820,000-tonne-per-year SAF facility in Rotterdam, citing rising costs and uncertain margins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To put things in perspective, the world's total SAF production capacity today stands at around 600 million litres a year, less than what airlines consume in a single day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To meet the ICAO target of 5% SAF by 2030, the global production output would need to increase 50-fold in just five years.

sections.label: Levy takings and off-take design
sections.summary: Levy takings will buy SAF at market prices, so off-take volume fluctuates with prices, ensuring cost stability for airlines and travellers but not volume stability for producers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The levy takings will be used to purchase SAF at market prices, meaning that the volume of off-take will fluctuate in response to price movements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This design ensures cost stability for airlines and travellers but not volume stability for producers.

sections.label: US SAF tax credits
sections.summary: The US Inflation Reduction Act introduced SAF tax credits of up to US$1.75 per gallon, unlocking billions in private investment across 14 states.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the US, the Inflation Reduction Act introduced SAF tax credits of up to US$1.75 per gallon, narrowing a price gap with conventional jet fuel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That single policy unlocked billions in private investment across 14 states, demonstrating how clear price and volume signals coupled with investment incentives can provide the certainty needed to scale production.

sections.label: Minimum offtake commitment
sections.summary: A minimum offtake commitment could help bridge that gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A minimum offtake commitment could help bridge that gap.

sections.label: SAF adoption and net-zero
sections.summary: SAF adoption is broadly recognised by the scientific community and industry as necessary for net-zero emissions by 2050 and Paris Agreement goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The adoption of SAF is broadly recognised by the scientific community and the industry as a necessary step in our pathway towards achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 and crucially, in striving to meet the Paris Agreement goals of limiting global warming to below two degrees Celsius.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports Bill intent
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the intent and broad purpose of this Bill, in line with scientific consensus on climate action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As a party that supports ambitious climate action in line with scientific consensus, the Workers' Party (WP) supports the intent and broad purpose of this Bill.

sections.label: SAF levy fund method questioned
sections.summary: The speaker asks why the Government chose a fund collecting SAF levies to procure SAF over other methods, if costs fall on consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If the costs are ultimately borne by the consumer, may I ask why has the Government chosen the method of establishing a fund for the collection of SAF levies to procure SAF over other methods?

sections.label: Public access to fund surplus
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the public will annually have access to information on the fund's surplus or slack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Given that the fund appears designed to have some slack after SAF purchases, which is prudent, will the public have access to information on how much surplus or slack there is in the fund annually?

sections.label: SAF levy cost and differentiation
sections.summary: The speaker asks for cost illustrations for a typical Changi passenger and whether the SAF levy will be differentiated by pollution levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Based on the current market rates for SAF and the projected adoption mandate, can the Government provide any illustration on the additional expected cost for a typical passenger flying of Changi Airport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Second, I note that the Bill allows for the possibility of prescribing different rates of SAF levy for different classes of passengers or cargoes, airports or aircraft, places of landing or any other differential basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask as a matter of equity and fairness, will the SAF levy be stratified or differentiated to charge those who pollute more such as private jets, special chartered flights or passengers on different classes of travel on commercial airlines and if so, how it will be done.

sections.label: Preventing carbon leakage after levy
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Government intends to prevent or significantly reduce carbon leakage after introducing the levy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Given the goal of net-zero future, how does the Government intend to prevent or significantly reduce such carbon leakage after the introduction of our levy?

sections.label: SAF levy schedule not fixed
sections.summary: The CAAS (Amendment) Bill does not prescribe a fixed schedule for increasing the SAF levy on blending ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The CAAS (Amendment) Bill does not prescribe a fixed schedule for increasing the SAF levy on blending ratio.

sections.label: Possible blending target triggers
sections.summary: A new blending target could be triggered by global certified SAF supply thresholds or SAF price premiums falling below a defined multiple of Jet A-1 fuel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For example, a new blending target could be triggered when global certified SAF supply reaches a certain threshold or once SAF price premiums fall below a defined multiple of Jet A-1 fuel.

sections.label: Passenger levies at Changi Airport
sections.summary: Passengers departing Singapore through Changi Airport pay $16.90 in levies, rising to between $19.90 and $32.90 with the SAF levy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Every passenger departing Singapore through Changi Airport will pay $16.90 for levies, that is $6.10 for Aviation levy and $10.80 for Airport Development Levy to CAAS, on top of the air ticket.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: With the SAF levy, the total levy per trip will increase to between $19.90 and $32.90, or an increase of between 18% and 95%, depending on the distance of the destination.

sections.label: Singapore sole passenger SAF levy
sections.summary: Singapore is the only country to have a SAF levy imposed solely on passengers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In fact, Singapore is the only country to have a SAF levy imposed solely on passengers.

sections.label: Blueprint SAF targets
sections.summary: The Singapore Sustainable Air Hub Blueprint has recommended a 1% SAF by 2026, rising to 3% to 5% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The Singapore Sustainable Air Hub Blueprint has recommended a 1% SAF by 2026, rising to 3% to 5% by 2030.

sections.label: Tuas refinery SAF production capacity
sections.summary: Following expansion of a renewable diesel refinery in Tuas, up to one million tonnes of SAF can now be produced per annum at the Singapore facility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Following the successful expansion of a renewable diesel refinery in Tuas, up to one million tonnes of SAF can now be produced per annum at the Singapore facility.

sections.label: SAF talent, fuel limits, emissions
sections.summary: Passage asks how SAFCo can secure oil trading talent and notes SAF's limited scalability, alternative pathways, ICAO standards, Malaysia's plant and aviation emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: How can SAFCo ensure they have the talents who have the expertise, experience and the market network of oil traders, who can trade on behalf of the airlines and seek best value for the SAF levy collected from passengers, which is likely to be in the tune of a few hundred million dollars per annum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: At present, it is the most mature and easy to use as it is a drop-in fuel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: However, its scalability is limited by the high price, which is, in turn, caused by limited feedstock.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: There are ongoing studies and trials on other pathways to reduce carbon emissions by airlines, such as hydrogen powered aircraft, battery operated aircraft for short-haul flights and contrail avoidance flight routes, and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In February 2016, ICAO announced the first global CO2 Standards for 13 new aircrafts launched after 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Malaysia has also opened a biofuel processing plant, facilitating potential regional trade in SAFs in the upcoming years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad that Singapore is joining in on this global movement to achieve net-zero emissions domestically and internationally in aviation emissions by 2050.The aviation industry is responsible for 2.5% of global emissions and SAFs can contribute around 65% reduction in emissions.

sections.label: US UK EU SAF legislation
sections.summary: Passage states the US, UK and EU have enacted legislation investing in second generation SAFs because HEFA biofuels are in limited supply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many global players, like the US, UK and the EU, have enacted specific legislations that invests in the development of second generation SAFs as the available biofuels currently made from the hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids (HEFA) process, are in limited supply.

sections.label: Biojet fuel cost comparison
sections.summary: Passage states research shows biojet fuel can be two to eight times more expensive than conventional kerosene jet fuel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Research has shown that biojet fuel can be two to eight times more expensive than conventional kerosene jet fuel.

sections.label: Levy impact on fares freight
sections.summary: Passage asks what the expected impact of the levy is on passenger fares and air freight costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What is the expected impact of the levy on passenger fares and also air freight costs?

sections.label: Indicative levy range confirmation
sections.summary: Passage asks whether the Government will confirm the publicly shared indicative levy range of around $3, $6 and $16 for short-, medium- and long-haul flights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To strengthen cost certainty, will the Government confirm that the indicative levy range shared publicly for the initial 1% target, around $3, $6 and $16 for short-, medium- and long-haul flights respectively, while noting that final amounts are likely to be even lower?

sections.label: Progressive levy for private jets
sections.summary: Passage asks whether the Ministry will commit to a progressive levy structure where private and business jets contribute more than regular families flying economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry commit to a progressive levy structure, where non-commercial, private and business jets contribute more than regular families flying economy?

sections.label: Levy and transit passengers
sections.summary: Asks the Minister of State to confirm the levy will not apply to transit or transfer passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister of State confirm that the levy will not apply to transit or transfer passengers?

sections.label: Changi fees and SAF levy
sections.summary: Asks whether adding a SAF levy after Changi's November 2024 fee rise risks pushing airlines to Bangkok or KLIA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Changi Airport raised passenger and airline fees in November 2024 to fund its $3 billion infrastructure plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If we now add a new SAF levy, will that risk pricing Singapore out of the regional race, pushing airlines toward Bangkok or Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA)?

sections.label: CAAS reporting and audits
sections.summary: Asks whether CAAS must publish an annual report, undergo independent audits, and whether a statutory review clause is considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will CAAS be required to publish a detailed annual report showing how much was collected, how much SAF was purchased, where it was sourced, who supplied it and how the SAF EAs were allocated?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the fund and its registry undergo independent audits, with findings made public?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And will the Ministry consider a statutory review clause, perhaps every three years, to assess whether the levy and fund remain effective and fit for purpose?

sections.label: CORSIA framework implementation
sections.summary: Asks the Minister of State to clarify when and how the CORSIA offsetting and penalty framework will be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister of State clarify when and how the CORSIA offsetting and penalty framework will be implemented, ideally through subsidiary legislation under the Air Navigation Act?

sections.label: Passenger burden for SAF
sections.summary: Asks the Minister of State to justify placing the financial burden on passengers rather than sharing risk with airlines or fuel suppliers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is accepted the high costs of SAF currently necessitates a measure and mechanism like this levy to support its initial adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, I remain concerned that this policy decision appears to place the financial burden entirely upon passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I respectfully ask the Minister of State to justify the approach and explain the considerations behind the choice, not to implement a model of financial risk sharing with airlines or fuel suppliers, or direct volume metric mandate on these commercial entities, an approach which has been adopted in other jurisdictions, such as EU and UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Flights from Singapore were previously estimated to increase by $3 to Bangkok; $6 to Tokyo and $16 to London.

sections.label: SAF cost and RSAF
sections.summary: States the Ministry said SAF costs more than three times conventional jet fuel, making it unsuitable for the RSAF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Ministry has previously stated, including in its discussion in 2023 that SAF is currently more than three times the cost of conventional jet fuel, thereby being unsuitable for use by the Republic of Singapore Air Force and its aircrafts, like the F-16.

sections.label: Singapore SAF use mandate
sections.summary: From next year, Singapore will be among the first countries and the first in Asia to mandate SAF use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: From next year, Singapore will be among the first countries and the first in Asia to mandate SAF use.

sections.label: Changi Airport passenger charges comparison
sections.summary: Changi passengers pay $65.20 in total charges, compared with other airports, and charges are projected to rise to $79.20 by 2030 before any SAF levy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Currently, departing passengers from Changi Airport are charged a total of $65.20, comprising of the passenger service and security fee, the aviation levy and the airport development levy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For KLIA, $23; Suvarnabhumi Airport in Bangkok, $30; Dubai International, $45; Incheon, $24.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Changi Airport's passenger charges are also projected to rise annually till 2030, reaching $79.20 before any SAF levy is added.

sections.label: Terminal 5 Changi capacity increase
sections.summary: With Terminal 5 coming online in the 2030s, Changi Airport's capacity will increase by 50 million passengers annually to nearly 140 million per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: With Terminal 5 coming online in 2030s, Changi Airport's capacity will increase by 50 million passengers annually, bringing total throughput to nearly 140 million passengers per year.

sections.label: Aviation contribution to Singapore economy
sections.summary: Singapore's aviation ecosystem contributes about 5% of GDP, supports over 190,000 jobs, and sustains about 529,000 jobs economy-wide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Singapore's aviation ecosystem, encompassing our airlines, airports, air navigation service providers and logistics partners, contributes about 5% of our gross domestic product and supports more than 190,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: When we include its wider economic impact through supply chains and tourism, aviation sustains about 529,000 jobs across our economy.

sections.label: SAF Fund levy rates
sections.summary: Clause 5 introduces section 25D, creating the SAF Fund financed by a levy estimated at $3, $6 and $16 for short-, medium- and long-haul flights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill introduces section 25D, creating the SAF Fund, financed by a levy estimated at $3 for short-haul, $6 for medium-haul and $16 for long-haul flights.

sections.label: Levy rates and policy questions
sections.summary: The proposed levy applies rates of $3, $6 and $16 by flight distance, with questions on passenger classes, cargo, and no timeline for price adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The proposed levy applies different rates by flight distance – $3, $6 and $16 depending on short-, medium- or long-haul flights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Will the levy be applied proportionately across the different passenger classes, so that it does not disproportionately burden economy class travellers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Likewise, how will the cargo sector be factored into this framework, given its integral role in Singapore's hub competitiveness?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We must monitor these developments carefully to ensure that the policy intent to encourage SAF adoption remains aligned with Singapore's long-term strategic goal of being a leading global and sustainable aviation hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I also note that no timeline has been specified for future price adjustments.

sections.label: SAF levy airfares
sections.summary: The Bill provides for an SAF levy, raising airfares from 2026, with proceeds buying SAF to reach 1% of jet fuel at Changi and Seletar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The SAF levy which this Bill provides for is one of Singapore’s policies that will contribute towards the global climate change mitigation effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It will mean that from 2026, travellers flying out of Singapore will pay slightly higher airfares.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Previous preliminary estimates from CAAS suggest that economy-class passengers may incur an additional $3 levy for flights to Bangkok, $6 for flights to Tokyo, $16 for flights to London.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The levy will be used to purchase SAF in bulk to achieve our target of 1% of all jet fuel used at Changi Airport and Seletar Airport in 2026.
